speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Education)
text: While not all of these competencies, such as collaboration skills and inventive thinking, can be measured through a single exam, they are developed in the course of learning the curriculum.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: One, how does the Ministry ensure that inquiry-based and collaborative learning approaches are not only present in the curriculum, but meaningfully integrated into classroom practice across all schools, including those serving lower-income or higher needs communities?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My second supplementary question, has the Ministry recently conducted comparative studies of other primary school education systems, particularly, any that have successfully balanced academic rigour with creativity and collaborations, and what lessons, if any, have been drawn from these systems?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: What collaborative learning, inquiry-based learning looks like will change, depending on whether it is talking about a mathematics class, a language class, a social studies class, and it will also change depending on the level of confidence and maturity of the students.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: What happens in the early primary years is going to look quite different from the later primary years.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, the core skillset to ensure that this type of pedagogy is available, used and integrated into our teaching methodologies, into all our classrooms, is there and is something that is at the heart of the teaching profession.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is a very robust community of practice amongst the educators within Singapore, and with our region and internationally.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They are constantly and consistently comparing notes on a practical level, on a personal level.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And there is also a robust community of practice in education research, which our educators and our education researchers participate in, and they are also comparing notes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we are always learning from one another.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To answer the second part of his second question, I think, would take me a Committee of Supply speech – to identify all the different components of pedagogy, learning methodology and faculty development.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I would assure Mr Tan and Members of the House that our education fraternity does not assume that we have solved all the problems, all the challenges within the education space, notwithstanding the ranking and grading, and external view, we have to consistently and regularly make sure that what we do in our schools and in our classrooms meets the needs, not just of the system, not just our general population of students, but the individual students that the educators hand-hold through their learning and development journey.
